newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ c/acct deficit seen at 5.5 pct/GDP by 1999.
newsitem.headline: NZ c/acct deficit seen at 5.5 pct/GDP by 1999.

text.p: New Zealand's 1997/98 budget released on Thursday showed the current account deficit rising to 5.5 percent of GDP by March 1999 from an estimated 4.5 percent in the year to March 1997.
Taking out the impact of high value-transport items would see a more modest rise in the deficit to 4.7 percent of GDP, the government said.
The current account deficit is seen at NZ$4.9 billion in 1997/98 (five percent of GDP), $5.7 billion in 1998/99 (5.5 percent of GDP) and $5 billion in 1999/00 (4.6 percent of GDP).
The government said a number of factors pointed to the current account position being sustainable, including the fact that New Zealand's deficit reflected rising investment rather than low savings.

However, the government said there was no guarantee financial markets would not be alarmed by a deficit over five percent of GDP. If this were to happen capital inflows would diminish, causing the dollar to depreciate.
This in turn would reduce the size of the current account deficit, but at the expense of potentially higher inflation and/or output, the government said.
